text:
maria: quick share — ran the cross-region quant snapshot for atlas13b across H100 / A100 / L40 in us-west and eu-west. TL;DR: fp8 gives ~1.6-1.9x speedup vs fp16 with <0.6% lm-perplexity regression on our eval set, int8 is faster but larger quality hits on long-context prompts. :bar_chart:

raj: nice. can you paste the perf table?

maria: pasted minimal CSV below (p50 latency ms, tokens/s throughput, quality delta = relative change in ppl). ran with fused_gemm_fp8 kernel where available.

```
region,gpu,mode,p50_ms,tokens_s,quality_delta
us-west,H100,fp16,46,980,-0.0%
us-west,H100,fp8,28,1650,-0.5%
us-west,H100,int8,24,1850,-1.8%
eu-west,A100,fp16,72,620,-0.0%
eu-west,A100,fp8,44,1050,-0.6%
eu-west,A100,int8,36,1250,-2.3%
us-west,L40,fp16,58,780,-0.0%
us-west,L40,fp8,40,1100,-0.7%
```

maria: note - int8 achieved best tokens/s but we saw some decode instability on longer (>2048) contexts in eu-west A100 run, likely kernel path mismatch.

sophia: what was the batch/seq mix? small requests or batching?

maria: 1-2 tok sampling workloads, mostly small requests (batch=1-4), seq mean 512. we used continuous batching with batcher target latency 80ms.

oliver: did you run the quant eval suite for semantic similarity and instruction-following? numbers above are ppl only.

maria: yes — quick summary: fp8 preserves instruction-following (ROUGE/F1 drop <0.5pts). int8 shows ~3pt drop on instruction F1 in rare cases (mainly numeric tables).

raj: kernel choices — you said fused_gemm_fp8 was used where available. which fallback triggered in eu-west?

maria: eu-west A100 hit a driver/torch mismatch so we fell back to matmul_generic_fp8 for two layers, causing the decode instability and higher memory. filed infra ticket to upgrade drivers.

eval-bot: perf-run 1754321999: artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-eval/1754321999/ — logs + traces + full eval CSV.

sophia: capacity guidance? if product wants 95th p50 ~50ms budget in us-west for small requests, what GPU fleet sizing?

maria: rough sizing: with fp8 on H100 expect ~20k tok/s per card at avg seq512 small-batch pattern, meaning ~1.8M tok/min ~ ~3600 requests/min (avg 500 tok/request). for fp16 you'd need ~1.2x-1.8x more cards depending on acceptable latency. int8 reduces card count but quality tradeoffs need manual review.

raj: any specific rollout guardrails? A/B or canary config?

maria: yes — recommend canary traffic on fp8 at 5% for 24h with instruction-following eval hooks and regression alert threshold: >1.0% ppl degradation or >1.5pt ROUGE drop triggers automatic rollback. also enable kernel fallback monitor for any matmul_generic hits.

oliver: sounds good. can we capture a compact playbook for SRE/infra to upgrade drivers in eu-west and re-run the A100 int8 path?
maria: on it — I'll open infra ticket and queue a re-run next deploy window. putting notes + raw logs in the artifact path. :memo:

sophia: thanks — this is actionable. fp8 looks like best middle ground for production: big perf win, tiny quality hit. int8 for batch offline or experiments only until we iron decode flakiness. :thumbsup:
